raw.body:
I tried to reproduce this so I could write a regression test to go with the proposed fix, and so far I can't get the track to break for plain object roots. Posting what I tried in case it helps narrow down the missing ingredient.

**1. React repo source tests** (current `main`, DEV, `enableComponentPerformanceTrack` on, `react-server-dom-webpack` test harness with `console.timeStamp`/`performance.measure` spied): payload shapes `{slot: <Greeting/>}`, multi-slot `{a, b}`, nested `{a: {b: element}}`, async components in slots, and all of those again with a `debugChannel` wired between server and client. The `Server Components ⚛` entries are logged for every shape, including plain object roots.

**2. Published `react-server-dom-webpack@19.3.0-canary-28cd4bb0-20260723`** (the exact version in the report): rendered payloads with `server.edge`'s `renderToReadableStream` and replayed them through `client.browser`'s `createFromReadableStream` under jsdom, with the payload split across two enqueues so chunks pass through the PENDING state, clocks aligned between the server and client processes, and `console.timeStamp`/`performance.measure` spied. Tested element root, `{slot: element}`, `{slot: Promise.resolve(element)}`, and an async-component slot; each with and without a `debugChannel` at different delivery timings. The component entries are logged in all of them — e.g. `RESULT object: ["Greeting"]`.

Why the read-site guard didn't bite in these flows: for a plain object root, `moveDebugInfoFromChunkToInnerValue` never moves the debug info off the chunk, so at flush time `root._debugInfo` is still non-empty and the recovery branch never runs. For the type restriction to matter, something must have emptied the chunk's `_debugInfo` while the object value carries one — and I couldn't find a code path in the client that attaches `_debugInfo` to a plain object (the attach sites — `moveDebugInfoFromChunkToInnerValue`, `addAsyncInfo`, the lazy/element paths — are all guarded by the same four types, and late debug rows for already-initialized chunks are dropped in `resolveDebugModel`).

Could you check what state the failing case is actually in — e.g. at the patched line in Waku, log `root.status`, `root._debugInfo.length`, and `root.value?._debugInfo` when the track is missing? Or share a repro outside Waku? One thing I couldn't rule out is Waku's SSR pass / double consumption of the payload, or the ws debug transport timing. Happy to turn a confirmed repro into a regression test + fix.
